answer: Practically, the chain should require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because vault only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, trellis is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any bridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
